newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says weak management impacting economy.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says weak management impacting economy.

text.p: Vietnam said on Monday it had maintained high growth rates in 1996, but conceded that poor management in some areas was hindering the economy.

State dailies carried details of a cabinet meeting which ended on Saturday, at which ministers were told that gross domestic product growth had reached 9.5 percent, while industry grew 14 percent and agriculture 4.8 percent.
But the reports, casting a picture of gloom, also pointed to what were described as "many shortcomings and weaknesses".

The Communist Party's Nhan Dan newspaper said unwillingness by government workers to take individual responsibility, poor coordination between government departments and unscientific work methods were to blame.
The paper, and others, also pointed to inefficient checking and control mechanisms and weak systems of gathering and analysing economic information, but gave no details.
Vietnam has recorded impressive economic growth rates since reforms were launched in the late 1980s.
Hanoi also appears to be winning a battle to rein in inflation, which stood at an annual rate of 4.5 percent in December from double digit levels a year earlier.
But the picture of an economic boom is being tarnished by problems, among which is a record trade deficit which reached $4.0 billion last year.

International economists and agencies say Vietnam needs to accelerate its reform process, promote trade liberalisation and the non-state sector, and make fundamental changes to the information environment in order to maintain competitiveness and growth.
